title: ci(fleet-write): grant permission-contents: write to the mint step so the relay can arm auto-merge
body:
Fixes #19762

## What changed

Touches `.github/workflows/**`, so this is a draft the maintainer merges by hand.

1. **The mint step grants `permission-contents: write`.** In `.github/workflows/fleet-write.yml`, `actions/create-github-app-token@v2` gains `permission-contents: write` beside the three existing `permission-*` inputs, with a comment naming the one consumer — GitHub's `enablePullRequestAutoMerge` / `disablePullRequestAutoMerge` mutations require `contents: write` on the token (measured on the relay's first live `automerge_enable`: "Resource not accessible by integration") — and stating that the op table has no contents op, so the grant is spent only by those two mutations. The header's permission list says the same.
2. **The op table spends it truthfully.** `PERMISSIONS` in `scripts/pm/fleet-write/ops.mjs` gains `contents: 'write'`; the `automerge_enable` and `automerge_disable` rows carry `permission: 'contents'`, so the validator's permission read stays a true statement of what each row spends. The header paragraph on permissions is updated.
3. **Self-tests** (`validate.mjs --self-test`, the refused-by-construction battery, 9 → 14 pinned cases): the map is exactly `issues` / `pull-requests` / `contents` write and `metadata` read; the two auto-merge rows spend `contents`; no other row does; every `contents` spender is an auto-merge GraphQL mutation, never a REST path; and the workflow's `permission-*` inputs, read from the file on disk, mirror `PERMISSIONS` exactly — a grant added on one side without the other reds.
4. **Nothing else.** No new op, no change to the sender gate, caps, ceilings, the executor or the four write tools.

Each was run alone with its exit code captured before any pipe; all 54 exited 0. `--ran` with the codes recorded: `54 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 54 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 54 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3)`. The live grant itself cannot be proven before merge (a workflow change runs only once it is on `main`); the card's post-merge verification is the director seat's: a two-action relay request (`pr_draft` + `pr_ready`, or `automerge_enable` on the next queued PR) reading back `enabledBy` = `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
